title: Powered pump units for vacuum cups, powered vacuum cup devices, and methods for applying a vacuum to a vacuum cup

features.item: cordless handheld vacuum lifting device with integrated battery power
features.quote: Battery powered hand-held vacuum cups have become popular in the auto glass industry for several reasons, including their ability to maintain suction to the cup part continuously during operation, even when the user releases the vacuum cup device to perform
features.note: The reference describes a battery-powered handheld vacuum cup, which implies cordless operation and integrated battery power.
features.refuted: The quote mentions 'battery powered hand-held vacuum cups' but does not explicitly state 'lifting device' or 'integrated battery power' in a way that confirms the assertion fully.

features.item: flexible sealing lip on suction cup that bounds sealed region against workpiece
features.quote: The cup part 101 is formed from resilient and flexible material with a concave surface facing away from the handle to which the cup part is connected.
features.note: The reference mentions a flexible cup part that forms a vacuum, but does not explicitly describe a distinct flexible sealing lip bounding the sealed region against a workpiece.

features.item: electric vacuum pump mounted within rigid body to draw air from sealed region
features.quote: The vacuum pump 604 shown schematically in FIG. 6 is also mounted on the pump unit housing 302 and includes a vacuum port 605 and a discharge port 608.
features.note: The reference describes an electric vacuum pump mounted on a pump unit housing, which is part of the rigid body, to draw air.
features.refuted: The quote states the vacuum pump is mounted on the 'pump unit housing' and includes ports, but does not explicitly state it is mounted 'within a rigid body to draw air from a sealed region.'

features.item: pressure sensor monitoring vacuum level in sealed region
features.note: The reference does not mention a pressure sensor or any means for monitoring the vacuum level.

features.item: warning indicator activated when vacuum falls to threshold above release vacuum level
features.note: The reference does not describe any warning indicator or its activation based on vacuum levels.

features.item: warning threshold defined relative to load-release vacuum rather than working vacuum
features.note: The reference does not describe any warning thresholds or how they are defined.

features.item: warning indicator remains active while grip vacuum persists below threshold
features.note: The reference does not describe any warning indicators or their behavior regarding persistence.

features.item: rechargeable battery integrated into rigid body powering vacuum pump
features.quote: The batteries 601 may include rechargeable batteries and the powered pump unit 300 may also include a battery charging circuit 1201 having a battery charging port 1202 as shown in FIG. 12.
features.note: The reference explicitly states that rechargeable batteries can be used and are integrated into the pump unit housing to power the vacuum pump.

features.item: warning indicator positioned on rigid body for visibility during lifting operation
features.note: The reference does not describe any warning indicators or their positioning.

features.item: single-hand portable design with all components carried by rigid body without external hose or cord
features.quote: Battery powered hand-held vacuum cups have become popular in the auto glass industry for several reasons, including their ability to maintain suction to the cup part continuously during operation, even when the user releases the vacuum cup device to perform
features.note: The reference describes a 'hand-held' and 'battery powered' vacuum cup, implying a self-contained, portable design without external hoses or cords.
features.refuted: The quote mentions 'hand-held vacuum cups' but does not explicitly state 'single-hand portable design' or 'all components carried by rigid body without external hose or cord.' It only implies portability and self-containment.

overall.why: The reference describes a battery-powered, handheld vacuum cup with an integrated electric pump and rechargeable battery, which aligns with several core features of the subject invention, but lacks details on vacuum monitoring and warning systems.
